findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the coffee maker diffuser is encrusted with soils. Discussed with PIC. Ensure that coffee makers are cleaned regularly enough to keep them clean. Inspector will return 01/01/2026 to re-inspect the coffee maker.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment: Inspector observed several foods to be out of temperature in a cooler at the facility. Food were Milk (47F), Lunchables (48F), Butter (47F), Sausage (46F), Cheese (46F), Egg (47F). Facility voluntarily discarded all foods. Ensure that all foods are stored at 41F or below. Inspector will return 12/26/2025 to re-inspect the coolers.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the walk-in cooler to be holding foods at or above 46F. For food, see violation 22. Ensure that all cold-holding units are capable of storing food at 41F or below. Inspector will return 01/01/2026 to re-inspect the cooler.
findings.citation_text: 4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment:
Inspector observed two trays at the coffee station to contain food debris. Discussed with PIC. Ensure that these trays are cleaned regularly enough to keep them clean.

Inspector observed the soda machine to be soiled with food debris next to soda nozzles and then on outside of the ice chute. Ensure that these areas are cleaned regularly enough to keep them clean.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(B) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the microwave to be cracked and chipping on the inside surfaces. Discussed with PIC. Ensure the microwave is replaced to render surfaces smooth, durable, and easily cleanable.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.113: Maintenance tools such as brooms, mops, vacuum cleaners, and similar items shall be: (A) Stored so they do not contaminate FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES; and (B) Stored in an orderly manner that facilitates cleaning the area used for storing the maintenance tools. 

The mop is observed stored in dirty water in the back of the facilty. Mop storage was discussed and the mop moved during this inspection to correct.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-101.11: (A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. Areas subject to moisture must be Nonabsorbent. (B) In TEMPORARY FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, floor may be material effectively treated to control dust and mud. Walls and ceilings may be material that protects interior from weather and windblown dust and debris. 

The hand sink in the bathroom is pulling away from the wall and exposing a gap. Repair the sink/wall so that it is a smooth and easily cleanable surface.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment: 3-302.11: Observed cartons of eggs to be stored on shelving above milk. Move egg cartons to the bottom shelf so they are stored UNDER ready-to-eat foods. (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). COS- discussed with PIC. Cartons moved.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.comment:
4-101.11: Durable, nonabsorbent, and CORROSION-RESISTANT (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness (D) SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, scratching, decomposition, and distortion. 

In various areas of the cold storage, cardboard is being used as shelf liner. Cease practice of using cardboard as liners. Shelf liners must be smooth and easily cleanable materials. Will check at next routine inspection.

findings.title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
findings.comment:
2-102.11: Based on the RISKS inherent to the FOOD operation, PIC shall demonstrate knowledge by:  (A) Having no Priority Foundation items; (B) Being a CFM; OR (C) Responding correctly questions as they relate to the specific FOOD operation. The areas of knowledge include C1 through C16.

PIC did not display knowlege of sanitizers/nor were sanitizers present in facility at time of inspection. See violations 16 and 48. When inspector inquired abut sanitizing agent for counters and surfaces, a gel hand sanitizer was presented. Hand sanitizer is not acceptable for sanitizing food contact surfaces.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). (3) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by cleaning visibly soiled containers, removing damaged containers, separating washed and unwashed produce (C).

REPEAT. Cartons of eggs stored above milk, deli meat, and cheese. Ensure eggs are stored in lowest shelf to prevent contamination of other food items in the event of a spill. PIC placed eggs on lowest shelf during inspection.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitzers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on devide and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)

*REPEAT*No sanitizer for food contact surfaces present at facility. Ensure chlorine or quaternary ammonium sanitizer equipped to sanitize food contact surfaces is present in facility by follow up date. Labeling should include: EPA registration label, directions for PPM sanitation, instructions for destruction of pathogens on food contact surfaces. Inspector will return by close of business to ensure item is corrected.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
4-302.14: A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided.

See violation #16. Test strips for sanitizer must be available for use. Test strips should correspond to the chemical in use. For example: Chlorine test strips should be bought for bleach; and quaterary ammonium test strips should be bought for quaternary ammonium sanitizer. Will follow up by close of business.
